claims.text: Large language models exhibit strong calibration at the token level when evaluating true/false statements or selecting answers in multiple-choice questions.
Open-ended generation tasks can be reformulated into token-level prediction tasks to leverage token-level calibration for self-evaluation.

evidence.description: LLMs have demonstrated strong calibration at the token level, particularly when choosing correct answers in multiple-choice questions or evaluating true/false statements.
We reformulate open-ended generation tasks into token-level prediction tasks, and leverage LLMs' superior calibration at the token level.

methodologies.name: Token-level Self-Evaluation for Selective Generation
methodologies.description: Reformulates open-ended generation into token-level prediction tasks using multi-way comparison or point-wise evaluation to score uncertainty and perform selective generation.

limitations.text: Sequence-level probability estimates given by LLMs, such as perplexity, are unreliable indicators of generation quality.
